title.purpose: Project subheads, decisions, and timeline roles.

label.purpose: Short technology, date, route, and metadata annotations.

shadows.name: device-lift
shadows.purpose: Frontmost overlapping app screen only; never paired with a decorative border.

shadows.name: pressed-control
shadows.purpose: Optional active-state feedback for a filled button.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single highest-priority action in a content group.
components.css: .ds-button-primary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 12px 18px; border: 0; border-radius: 6px; background: #0866C6; color: #FFFFFF; font: 600 1rem/1.2 "Source Sans 3", "Segoe UI", sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1), transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-button-primary:hover { background: #064A91; } .ds-button-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); } .ds-button-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0866C6; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: A lower-emphasis action such as résumé download.
components.css: .ds-button-secondary { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; justify-content: center; padding: 11px 17px; border: 1px solid #171A1D; border-radius: 6px; background: transparent; color: #171A1D; font: 600 1rem/1.2 "Source Sans 3", "Segoe UI", sans-serif; text-decoration: none; transition: background-color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1), color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-button-secondary:hover { background: #171A1D; color: #FFFFFF; } .ds-button-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0866C6; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Active Navigation Link
components.description: Compact navigation state with a structural Flutter-blue rule.
components.css: .ds-nav-link { position: relative; display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; color: #4B5158; font: 600 0.95rem/1 "Source Sans 3", "Segoe UI", sans-serif; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav-link::after { position: absolute; right: 0; bottom: 7px; left: 0; height: 2px; background: #0866C6; content: ""; transform: scaleX(0); transform-origin: left; transition: transform 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-nav-link:hover, .ds-nav-link-active { color: #171A1D; } .ds-nav-link:hover::after, .ds-nav-link-active::after { transform: scaleX(1); } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0866C6; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Technical Label
components.description: A short engineering annotation, never a body-copy style.
components.css: .ds-technical-label { color: #4B5158; font: 500 0.75rem/1.4 "IBM Plex Mono", Consolas, monospace; letter-spacing: 0.02em; }

components.name: Case Study Link
components.description: An inline route link with an always-visible affordance.
components.css: .ds-case-link { display: inline-flex; min-height: 44px; align-items: center; gap: 8px; color: #0866C6; font: 600 1rem/1.2 "Source Sans 3", "Segoe UI", sans-serif; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 4px; text-decoration-line: underline; transition: color 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1), gap 180ms cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1); } .ds-case-link:hover { gap: 12px; color: #064A91; } .ds-case-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0866C6; outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview: A recruiter is reviewing Muhammad's work in daylight on a laptop, then reopening a case study on a phone before an interview. The interface should feel like a well-organized product workshop: large working screens, concise annotations, precise dividers, and implementation notes placed where they help someone understand a decision. The light canvas is practical and calm; dark sections appear only when they improve screenshot contrast or mark a deliberate change in project atmosphere. This is editorial in pacing, not in magazine costume. The system uses a twelve-column layout and strong typography, but avoids the saturated display-serif-plus-mono aesthetic.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white canvas with charcoal type and a restrained Flutter-blue signal.
Asymmetric twelve-column compositions with obvious reading order.
Real Flutter screens at meaningful sizes; no illustrative substitutes.
Thin rules, square-ended spacing rhythm, moderate radii, and very little elevation.
Mobile-interface transitions used to explain sequence, not decorate text.
Truthful content centralized in one data model and reused across preview and case-study routes.

rules.name: The Ten-Percent Signal Rule
rules.body: Flutter blue and aqua together occupy no more than roughly ten percent of a viewport. Their rarity makes active states legible.

rules.name: The Aqua Context Rule
rules.body: Bright aqua is interactive on dark surfaces or non-textual on light surfaces. Use aqua-deep for normal-size text on the canvas.

rules.name: The No-Gradient Rule
rules.body: Color changes by section, state, or solid block—not through decorative gradients or gradient text.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Bricolage speaks; Source Sans explains. IBM Plex Mono only annotates.

rules.name: The One-Display Rule
rules.body: Each viewport gets one dominant heading. Supporting headings step down clearly instead of competing at hero scale.

rules.name: The Flat-by-Default Rule
rules.body: If a surface is understandable with spacing and a rule, adding a shadow is prohibited.

rules.name: The One-Lift Rule
rules.body: No viewport contains more than one visibly elevated screenshot group.

dos: **Do** let real Flutter screens be the largest proof on the page and capture them from the actual running projects or Muhammad's supplied devices.
**Do** use the twelve-column grid asymmetrically while preserving a clear mobile reading order.
**Do** keep body copy within 68ch, headings balanced, and technical labels short.
**Do** keep Flutter blue and aqua controlled, verify contrast, and use aqua-deep when aqua-family text appears on the light canvas.
**Do** use thin rules, 6–16px interface radii, deliberate whitespace, and flat surfaces.
**Do** preserve /resume.pdf, canonical contact links, verified repositories, the authentication-only PalPath web deployment, React/Vite/Tailwind, and Vercel deployment behavior.
**Do** provide semantic HTML, keyboard navigation, stable accessible names, visible focus, descriptive alt text, intrinsic image dimensions, and reduced-motion fallbacks.
**Do** omit a link, image, metric, role, or feature when it cannot be verified.
donts: **Don't** use giant gradient headings, purple-to-blue gradients, gradient text, glassmorphism, glowing borders, random background particles, decorative grid backgrounds, or empty grey project-image placeholders.

**Don't** build a huge centered SaaS hero, hero-metric template, fake statistics, “24/7 learning” counters, skill percentage bars, proficiency dots, fabricated testimonials, clients, achievements, or performance claims.
**Don't** use floating technology pills, repeated identical card grids, cards nested inside cards, excessive rounded cards, or large icon tiles above every heading.
**Don't** repeat tiny uppercase tracked eyebrows or numbered section markers as page scaffolding.
**Don't** use generic rocket, sparkle, brain, or lightning icons, hand-drawn SVG scenes, decorative stripes, or stock illustrations as substitutes for app evidence.
**Don't** overuse IBM Plex Mono; it is reserved for technical labels and metadata.
**Don't** use constant parallax, magnetic interactions, bounce or elastic easing, continuous WebGL/canvas effects, or animate every text element.
**Don't** use generic copy such as “turning ideas into reality,” the title “Aspiring Software Engineer,” or position Muhammad as a generic full-stack, Node.js, backend, AI, or GenAI engineer.
**Don't** pair a one-pixel border with a wide decorative shadow, exceed 16px radii on ordinary cards/sections, hide content until an animation fires, clip focus rings, or allow horizontal overflow.
